title: The Cellar of Marrow Creek
premise: Isandro Ravensworth hosts a dead-of-night radio show from her family's farmhouse, taking calls from listeners who died the week before — a gift she inherited from her grandmother, who vanished in 1974. When every mirror in the house begins reflecting one second late, Isandro realizes the delay is the house counting down, and that her grandmother didn't disappear: she took something from Marrow Creek's drowned cellar and never gave it back. To stop the lag from swallowing her own reflection, Isandro must descend into the flooded cellar, return what was taken, and choose between keeping her place in the town that needs her voice or telling the truth about what the Ravensworths did. She returns the stolen bell of the creek, losing the show but gaining a real belonging — and one final call comes through, from her grandmother, finally at rest.
about_author: Sable Fairweather is the pen name of a former late-night radio producer who spent years answering calls from strangers who sounded like ghosts. She writes horror about small towns, old houses, and the debts families never finish paying.

chapters.title: The Second Behind the Glass
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. During her broadcast, callers describe their own funerals with unsettling accuracy, and afterward she notices a mirror lagging a full second behind her movements. She counts the doors out of habit and finds thirteen where there should be twelve. The emotional beat is creeping dread: her safe ritual of control over the dead begins to feel like something controlling her.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Buried
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, intercut with 1974 letters from her grandmother Odile. Searching the attic, Isandro finds letters hinting Odile stole a bell from the drowned cellar beneath Marrow Creek to power the family's gift — and that the townspeople's loyalty was bought with silence. Her neighbor Hal, whose father was there in '74, warns her to leave it buried. The beat is loyalty versus truth tightening around her.

chapters.title: Thirteen Doors Open
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The lag spreads to every reflective surface; her own reflection starts moving independently, mouthing her name. The thirteenth door appears in the hallway and opens onto the flooded cellar stairs. Hal confesses his father helped hide the theft, and the town's devotion to the Ravensworths curdles into menace when they gather outside demanding she stay quiet. The beat is betrayal and isolation at peak pressure.

chapters.title: Return What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She descends into the drowning dark, finds the bell's empty cradle and Odile's remains still holding it, and rings it once underwater — returning the sound the creek lost in 1974. The mirrors snap true; the doors return to twelve; the show goes silent forever. In the epilogue-quiet aftermath, the radio crackles with one last caller: Odile, saying thank you. The beat is grief transmuted into belonging.
